title: Array Partition
statement: The array `nums` holds an even number of integers, `2n`. Split all of them into `n` pairs so that every element belongs to exactly one pair. Each pair contributes the smaller of its two values, and the score of a split is the total of these contributions. Return the largest score any split can reach.
notes:
## Intuition

Whatever a pair's larger value is, it is thrown away; only the smaller one counts. So every pair "wastes" its larger element, and the goal is to waste as little as possible. The very largest value can never count (it is the bigger one in its pair), so the best it can do is protect the second largest by pairing with it. Repeating that argument from the top down pairs neighbours in sorted order. Trying every pairing would also work, but the number of pairings grows faster than factorially.

## Approach

1. Sort `nums` in increasing order.
2. Pair positions `0`-`1`, `2`-`3`, and so on; in each pair the element at the even index is the smaller.
3. Add up the values at even indices `i` into `total`.
4. Return `total`.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [1, 4, 3, 2]` sorts to `[1, 2, 3, 4]`. With `i = 0`, `total` becomes `1` (pair `(1, 2)`). With `i = 2`, `total` becomes `1 + 3 = 4` (pair `(3, 4)`). The loop ends and the answer is `4`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n log n): the sort dominates; the scan is linear.
- Space: O(1) beyond the sort, which works in place.

## Pitfalls

- Sort numerically with `(a, b) => a - b`; JavaScript's default sort compares strings and misorders negatives and multi-digit numbers.
- Step `i` by 2, not 1: each pair is counted once, through its smaller element.
- Negative values do not change the argument; the same sorted pairing is still optimal.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `nums` | the input, sorted in place |
| `total` | sum of the smaller values of the pairs so far |
| `i` | even index of the smaller element of the current pair |

narration.1: The function receives the 2n numbers that must be split into pairs.
narration.2: Sort the numbers so that neighbours in the array become the pairs.
narration.3: Start the running score at zero.
narration.5: Visit every even index; each one starts a new pair of neighbours.
narration.6: The element at the even index is the smaller of its pair, so it is the one that counts.
narration.8: Every pair has been counted; return the score.
